items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: That was a girl vocalist with the group. Her name was Linda something, I don't know, and she liked me, you know.

ctx.x: What was it like working with Fletcher Henderson's band in Mississippi? You said you couldn't wait to get out of there and didn't want to go back.

Oh, boy, oh, boy. Well, I'll give you an idea. I was in a little town, Rosedale we stopped, and I went into a little place to get a sandwich, so there was an old white man in there, and there was just the two of us. Nobody -- as a matter of fact no one was in there but him, and I went in and I ordered a ham sandwich, and I think a pork sandwich, and he started cutting the meat, slowly, you know. He was very -- I could see him thinking, I could see the wheels turning. This was an old man. So he finally just stuck…

That was a girl vocalist with the group. Her name was Linda something, I don't know, and she liked me, you know. So we played a town called Tupelo, Mississippi, and this girl had to -- she was a very attractive girl, she was a mulatto girl, you know, very light.
